verdict_note: The sign-off is for the branch head 138c4d9d (12424fcc plus the laws/M3 re-derivation). It is not for 12424fcc alone, where M1 breaks the M3 gate. The class is sound: trace_bound writes ordinary Bend files, and Bend decides each one. The committed proof passes bend and BendTT --verdict, and both refuse a planted change. The class regenerates the proof byte for byte under three hash seeds. It names no law, contract or target, and uses no escape hatch. It also proves the second claim C_o12_open and returns None on C_o12_tight. Every prediction reproduces except what the local GENV blocks. P1 and P2 hold here, and CI runs o12-p1-p2 green with the pinned checker. P3 and P4 were replayed in copies: holon and the instrument agree on G10 at every step, each Bend re-check passes, and CI runs o12-p3 and o12-p4 green. R2 and R3 held at 12424fcc. There is one major finding (M1). Rule P11 makes M3's derivation list every law file of M0-M2, so the new M2 law put laws/M3/DERIVATION.json and REGISTRY.json out of date, and gate-M3-G2 failed on 12424fcc. Commit 138c4d9d regenerates both files with holon derive. That resolution is the right one, and it makes I65-R2 and I65-R3 miss, which the report must score as missed. The eleven minor findings are about reporting, robustness and stale pins. None of them makes a recorded status untrue. Two conditions carry over from the prereg and still apply. The merge waits for I66 (Q62): gate-M2 fails only GEVID, on the derived law, as preregistered. CI on 138c4d9d had not started when this review was written, so the M3 gate at that head is confirmed here only by a local re-derivation. That re-derivation is the comparison G2's I30 part makes; a full local G2 on M3 did not finish. docs/iterations/I65.md is not written yet. The commit that adds it must touch only I65's outcome paths, because it ends R2's window.

findings.why:
The prereg cannot keep both of these claims once an M2 law is added: R3 ("no commit of I65's own changes a law ... of M3") and R1's M3 clause ("the M3 gate's failing items are those of the base"). The prereg and both of its reviews missed the cross-milestone input. Its list of files shared with I26 names neither laws/M3 file. At 12424fcc, R1 misses, because I65 adds a failing M3 gate item (G2). At 138c4d9d, R2 and R3 miss. Judgment on the resolution: 138c4d9d is right.
  - The two files are regenerated by their generator, as AGENTS rule 4 requires, and the change is confined to derivation metadata.
  - It restores the M3 gate for both lanes.
  - It reports the miss rather than hiding it.
Each rejected alternative was rightly rejected:
  - Merging with M3's G2 red breaks the base for every lane.
  - Putting the change in a merge commit, or after the commit that adds I65.md, games R2 and R3. test_o12.own_commits reads `git log --first-parent --no-merges` only up to that commit.
  - Exempting contract laws from P11 edits holon/rules, which O4 forbids. It also bends M3's derivation semantics to fit the prereg, against the spirit of AGENTS rule 2.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_o12.py:740-769 (TestMachinery.test_the_differential_keeps_the_mark, test_refute_keeps_the_mark); holon/refute_m3.py:817 (the solver pin is checked before every stage, --only filter included); .github/workflows/holon-i65-suites.yml on the CI-only branch (set +e ... exit 0)
findings.what:
Neither R4 check has a fully green run anywhere. In CI's o12-machinery (pinned bend), both fail with 'holon refute: the pinned solver is not installed as pinned: no solver binary at /root/.holon/tools/extract/bin/z3'. The job's check still reads success, because the suites workflow ends every job with exit 0: its log says 'FAILED (failures=2)', 'exit 1'. Locally (z3 present, GENV failing) the substance holds:
  - test_refute_keeps_the_mark passes;

A replay in a copy also holds: `holon differential --milestone M2 --reuse-view` ends with 'contracts on M2: C_o12 proved (marks L_undo_cancel)'. findings.where: holon/gen/trace_bound.py:1352-1361 (catches only Fail), :1028 (2^n case split); holon/mpipeline.py:811 and :906-913 (the GENERATORS loop catches only Unsupported, IRError and OracleError), :1250 (decide_negation catches nothing); compare holon/gen/implication.py:205
findings.what:
Two robustness gaps.
  - trace_bound() converts only its own Fail into None. Any other exception escapes the generator loop and aborts `holon run` for the whole milestone: a KeyError from a malformed sidecar entry, a FactsError from Machine.ex, an AttributeError. implication.py, by contrast, records a crashing untrusted generator as no proof.
  - bool_helper splits every Bool atom of the goal and of every invariant conjunct with itertools.product, with no bound. A class-shaped law with about 20 atoms emits 2^20 cases per helper per action and stalls the run.
Neither is reachable today: of all committed laws, only L_contract_C_o12 gets past parse(). About 30 class-shaped probes over the view gave only Fail or a proof. Bend refused the false probe (W <= g at s0) and accepted the true ones (t <= t + g, (b) alone, an ite term).
findings.why: The class is appended last to GENERATORS. It is tried on every IR 0.3 law no earlier class proves, on negations, and on implication obligations, so a latent crash or blow-up would take whole runs down, not just one law.
findings.fix: Wrap TraceBound(...).render() in trace_bound() with `except Exception: return None` (or record the error as implication.py does). Fail when the atom count exceeds a fixed bound, for example 12.

findings.where: holon/gen/trace_bound.py:792-840 (list_component), :1073-1135 (le), :37-38 (NAT_CMP, BOOL_OPS), :484 (decision_lemma's unused `inline`); pyflakes: unused locals at :345, :474, :852; tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O2
findings.what:
O2 promises lemmas the class does not have.
  - O2 says each comparison is carried by list lemmas for 'snoc, take, drop, tail, the target library's nth_default and set_default builtins'. The class has no tail lemma.
  - A set_default effect is carried only at a point read (read_rule), never under the quantified Nat binder. Probe: 'for every k, nth_ch(chs, k).s <= t' Fails with "list effect ['call', 'set_ch', ...]", although LIBRARY's tb_set_at would carry it.
  - le() handles only <=. '<' and '==' comparisons are never carried (probes: t < t + g + 1, ver == ver), and NAT_CMP, which names '<', is dead.
C_o12 needs none of these: the view applies tail only to Nat lists the claim never reads.
findings.why: O2's escape clause ("a comparison it cannot carry gets no proof") keeps every outcome true. But the frozen contract text and the module docstring overstate what the class carries, which misleads the I33 work that is to reuse the class over M3.
findings.fix: Implement tail and set_default under the binder (tb_set_at already exists), or state the actual coverage in the module docstring and in I65.md. Remove the dead names.

findings.where: holon/__main__.py (derive: before_derive, rules.main, after_derive); holon/rules/__init__.py:774-776 (deletes every laws/<M>/L*.json the rules do not derive); holon/contracts.py:319-366 (before_derive validates only K1/K9; after_derive catches only OSError, ValueError, KeyError and TypeError); holon/contracts.py:33 ('2 refused, nothing written')
findings.what: `holon derive` is not atomic when the contract step fails. Reproduced in a copy: one action's guards in gen/M2/extracted/m1_view.json were made a string, which the rules never read. `holon derive --milestone M2` then ended in an uncaught AttributeError traceback from statement_hash inside registry_with. By then holon.rules had already deleted laws/M2/L_contract_C_o12.json and rewritten laws/M2/REGISTRY.json without the law.
findings.why: The docstrings promise a refusal with nothing written. A broken view leaves laws/M2 half-written instead: the law gone and the registry without it. G1 or G2 then report something other than the real cause.
findings.fix: Compute contract_laws and registry_with (the statement hashes included) in before_derive, before anything is written, and catch Exception in after_derive. Or let the rules write into a temporary directory and move the whole result into place.

findings.where: results/M2/L_contract_C_o12.json fields refinement_refs and kernels[lean4].reading; holon/records.py:455-474 (refinement_refs); holon/gen/lean_common.py:27-33 (READINGS['machine_oracle']); holon/gen/lean_machine.py:116 and :697 (I65 makes a machine_oracle model without parameters legal)
findings.what:
Two fields of the L_weak's record describe a different model.
  - refinement_refs lists replay/M2/report.json#/refinement/per_action/<a> for all ten actions. That replay ran 'the M2 model of spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json', the abstraction, never the view, whose commit, finalize, prove and setPause guards differ. refinement_refs checks facts for its per-edge records but not for the replay part, and this is the first M2 law over other facts.
  - The lean4 entry's reading describes 'the Fn<List<Nat>,Nat> oracle parameter' and site predicates. The view has neither.
findings.why: No gate reads either field today: GEVID does not read refinement_refs. But both read as evidence about the view, and I65's own prereg says the view's evidence is not computed before I66.
findings.fix: Say in I65.md that these refs belong to the abstraction's replay. In a later key, restrict the replay part of refinement_refs to laws whose facts are the replay's model, and give a parameterless machine_oracle model its own reading.

findings.what: The generated window bundle is the abstraction's bundle, re-keyed to whatever bytes the view has now. Nothing checks that the view is still the declaration's view of the current abstraction, as `holon differential --reuse-view` checks before it reuses one. resolve_bundle runs its unclassified-definition check only on the derived path, never on an exact match. So after a hand edit of the view (P4's W + 1), the record still reads ledger_match 'exact'. Today all 0 of the view model's definitions are unclassified under the generated bundle (recomputed), so nothing is hidden.
findings.why: O4 mandates the generated exact bundle. But 'exact' then means 'the abstraction's assumption profile, asserted of any document that names the declaration', with no check that the assertion still applies.
findings.fix: In _window_bundles or resolve_bundle, run unclassified() for a generated bundle, with the record's model text, and fall back to 'derived' (or refuse) when any definition is unclassified.

verified: Soundness of trace_bound. The final def Laws.l_contract_c_o12(p, k) is checked against the law statement holon.gen.mlaws emitted in LAWS.bend: Bend refuses a proof file that defines a Laws.* name, and refuses a law with no def. The PROOF imports exactly its LAWS.bend, and the core under gen/M2/core (unchanged since the prereg). It declares no law. bend.escape_hatches finds nothing, and there is no ?name, @unsafe, def f?() or foreign import. Every lemma, the pointwise ones included, is a def with a body that Bend checks; a probe confirmed that Bend refuses a non-decreasing self-call. trace_bound.py names no law, contract or target, and no model name in its logic (one comment at :595 cites HEntry as an example).
